description: Beam span divided by beam depth
source: Eurocode 2 Table 7.4N basic span/depth limits: 20 simply supported, 14 continuous (anbeal.co.uk/ec2spantodepth)
comments: Typical unchanged (12, stocky beam); max raised to 20 = EC2 limit for simply supported beams. Actual depth depends on load, so this stays a design assumption.

description: Beam width divided by beam depth
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Beam width is usually about half the depth (b = h/2, engineers use h/3 to 2h/3 as rule of thumb); narrower beams need more depth, wider ones clash with wall thickness. 0.4-0.6 spans the common range. | earlier note: No source found; b/h 0.4-0.6 is common practice. Left as team assumption.

source: EN 1991-1-1 Annex A: reinforced normal-weight concrete 25 kN/m3 (standard value, not re-checked online this session)
comments: Was 2400 (range 1920-2880 = +-20%, too wide for normal-weight concrete). Implied rebar ~150 kg/m3 = 6% of mass, consistent with the steel production row. | [2026-10-16] Range 2000-3000 -> 2400-2600: reinforced concrete density is well known (~2400-2500 kg/m3)

description: Amount of concrete per kg of product
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Rebar in RC beams is typically 100-250 kg per m3 of concrete; 150 kg/m3 at 2500 kg/m3 gives 6% steel and 94% concrete. Rebar content is a real uncertainty that changes the beam's footprint a lot (steel is ~10x more carbon-intensive per kg), so it now varies in the uncertainty analysis (shares are re-normalised). Concrete is the complement of steel: 0.90-0.96. | [2026-10-16] Fixed (was a +-20 % range): main component of the mixture; the steel share carries the uncertainty (independent +-20 % on both made the beam 0.8-1.2 kg per kg)

description: Amount of steel per kg of product
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): 150 kg rebar per m3 of concrete / 2500 kg per m3 = 6%. Range 100-250 kg/m3 = 4-10%. Stiffer/heavily loaded beams and shorter spans sit at the top of the range.

description: Amount of formwork per kg of product
source: recalculated for density 2500 kg/m3 ; derived from beam geometry, 10 reuses
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Plywood formwork reused ~10 times; 8.1 kg per 1875 kg beam at 6 m span (formula in the earlier note). Fixed because it is a geometric consequence of the reference span. | earlier note: fixed per kg of beam, exact at the 6 m reference span: formwork 6 x (2 x 0.5 + 0.25) m x 0.018 m x 600 kg/m3 / 10 reuses = 8.1 kg per 1875 kg of beam (6 m x 0.5 x 0.25 m x 2500 kg/m3) = 0.00432 kg/kg

description: Years the product lasts in use
source: EN 1990 design working life 50 y (class 3) to 100 y (class 4); SBR: service life of most concrete structural parts > 100 y (betonhuis.nl/beton-en-de-technische-levensduur)
comments: 75 = common building-life convention, kept as typical; range widened to 50-100.

description: kg of reinforced concrete beam (concrete + rebar, treated as a whole) that goes to waste reinforced concrete recycling at end of life, per kg of product
source: EU-27 non-hazardous C&D waste 2020-21: 80% recycling + 7% backfilling, 7% landfilling, 6% energy recovery (JRC131294, Use of recycled aggregates in concrete, p.10); NL 2012: 98% recovery, ~2% landfilled (EC CDW factsheet NL); rebar recovery 98% at demolition (Eurofer 2012 survey, steelconstruction.info)
comments: Whole beam treated as one stream (concrete + steel not split). Includes backfilling (7% of EU CDW), which has no separate activity here; EU mineral-only recycling+backfilling = 87/94 = 93% (energy-recovery share excluded), rounded down to 90% for reporting bias. Range: min ~ countries with 70-80% recovery, max ~ NL (98%).

description: kg of reinforced concrete beam (concrete + rebar, treated as a whole) that goes to waste concrete landfilling at end of life, per kg of product
source: EU-27 non-hazardous C&D waste 2020-21: 80% recycling + 7% backfilling, 7% landfilling, 6% energy recovery (JRC131294, Use of recycled aggregates in concrete, p.10); NL 2012: 98% recovery, ~2% landfilled (EC CDW factsheet NL); rebar recovery 98% at demolition (Eurofer 2012 survey, steelconstruction.info)
comments: Complement of recycling row (shares re-normalised to 100%). EU ~7%, NL ~2%; typical 10% kept conservative for whole-Europe scope. Beam's ~6% steel is landfilled with the concrete here (ecoinvent 'waste concrete' dataset).

description: Country whose electricity mix is displaced by energy recovered at end of life
comments: Common-sense estimate (Claude, for LCA-team review): Model choice, not a measurement: NL because the RAW project and its electricity/heat credit assumptions are Dutch and the ecoinvent NL grid is available. Only matters for the energy credit of incineration; change on study_setup if you model another country.
